content:
MacBook Neo has only been around for a few months, but it has already become a hit product for Apple. Reports indicate that its successor will launch next year, and the MacBook Neo 2 will feature the upgrade that most users have been hoping for: more memory.

The MacBook Neo 2 will come with 12GB of memory, up from 8GB in the current model.

When the MacBook Neo launched earlier this year, it delivered an impressively powerful Mac at an affordable price.

The price has gone up since then (unless you buy a refurbished unit from Apple), but the machine continues to prove itself capable of handling most computing tasks.

Unless you need to do heavy video editing, write code, or run AI models locally, the MacBook Neo should be more than enough for you. It can even handle 59 Chrome tabs simultaneously.

But if there's one single change Apple could make to the original MacBook Neo, I'd wager plenty of users would ask for more memory.

The MacBook Neo comes with an A18 Pro chip and 8GB of memory, but reports suggest the MacBook Neo 2 will feature an A19 Pro chip along with 12GB of memory.

An extra 50% of memory could make a huge difference for users worried about hitting spec limits.

8GB of memory performs far better on a Mac than on a PC. Since the current MacBook Neo has already proven itself sufficient for most users, its successor should be even more so.

The upgraded memory will also allow the MacBook Neo 2 to better take advantage of the new AI features in macOS 27—including some that require 12GB of memory.

Beyond the 50% more memory, combined with a more powerful chip, the MacBook Neo 2 should be enough to satisfy a wider range of users.

What limitations of the MacBook Neo are keeping you on another Mac model? Let us know in the comments.
